title: Understanding the Null Hypothesis
text: The null hypothesis states that the proportion of adults in Berkeley that consume at least $$1$$ soda every day is 72%. This is represented as $$p=0.72$$.

title: Sample Proportion
text: The sample proportion, denoted as \( \hat{\alpha} \), is the proportion of the sample that consumes at least $$1$$ soda every day. In this case, \( $$\hat{\alpha}=0.67$$ \).

title: Significance Level
text: The significance level is the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true. Here, the significance level is 10%, or $$0.10$$.

title: Decision Rule
text: To reject the null hypothesis, the sample proportion \( \hat{\alpha} \) must be significantly different from the hypothesized proportion $$(0.72)$$ at the 10% significance level.

title: Calculate the Test Statistic
text: Calculate the test statistic using the formula: \( z=\frac{\hat{\alpha}-p}{\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)}{n}}} \), where \( $$\hat{\alpha}=0.67$$ \), \( $$p=0.72$$ \), and \( $$n=1000$$ \).

title: Compare with Critical Value
text: Compare the calculated test statistic with the critical value for a two-tailed test at the 10% significance level.

title: Conclusion
text: Since the calculated test statistic is less than the critical value, we reject the null hypothesis.
